_comment: NRI-day rules for the Sea time screen (informational only, decisions.md R15). Thresholds live here, not in code, because Finance Acts change them. verified_by_owner stays false until the owner (or a tax professional) has checked the citation; the app then shows a 'not yet checked' note.

sources: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 6(1)(a): resident if in India for 182 days or more in the previous year.
Section 6(1), Explanation 1(a): for an Indian citizen who leaves India as a member of the crew of an Indian ship or for employment outside India, the 60-day test in clause (c) becomes 182 days.

Section 6(1), Explanation 2 and Income-tax Rules, 1962, rule 126 (from FY 2015-16): for crew of a ship on an eligible voyage, the days from the sign-on date to the sign-off date entered in the Continuous Discharge Certificate are not counted as days in India.
Income-tax Act, 2025 (in force from 1 April 2026) replaced the 1961 Act. The 182-day test is assumed to continue; the section numbers have NOT been checked yet.

notes: Only days between the sign-on and sign-off dates in your CDC count, and only on an eligible voyage (a ship carrying passengers or cargo in international traffic). Coastal voyages between Indian ports do not count.
Days you are not on board are counted as possibly in India, because the app does not know about trips abroad off the ship.

Other rules can make you resident anyway, for example the deemed-residency rule for Indian citizens with income from Indian sources above 15 lakh rupees who are not taxed in any other country (Finance Act 2020).
This is not tax advice. Check with a tax professional before filing your return.
